CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One

Definition, Understanding and Terminology Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a development system based on Children's rights through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's Rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

Article 43

1. Complaints of acts of violence against Women and Children as referred to in Article 42 may be made by reporters consisting of:
a. Victims;
b. Family;
c. Community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of protection of Women and Children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and
c. by letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 42 are authorized to handle victims of violence against Women and Children obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation

Article 47

1. The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence.
2. Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for Women and Children victims of violence who need safe houses include: a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or d. neglected if not placed in a safe house.
5. The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 10

1. The community shall and is responsible for implementing the protection of Women and Children including:
a. participation in prevention and providing support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting violations of the rights of Women and Children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervising the law enforcement process against cases of violations of the rights of Women and Children.
2. The responsibility of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) is in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

Paragraph 4

Social

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 58

1. The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Women and Child Protection.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out in the form of:
a. training for government officials and law enforcers on prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and
f. increasing the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent in conducting guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of Agency.

Paragraph 6

Social

Article 51

1. Repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return Women and Children victims of violence to their area of origin.
2. Repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
3. The Regency Government carries out repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 49

1. Law enforcement and legal assistance services are actions of law enforcement officers provided to Women and Children victims of violence and/or witnesses.
2. Law enforcement and legal assistance services as referred to in paragraph (1) are carried out by prioritizing the best interests of victims.

Article 24

Children in formal and non-formal educational institution environments must be protected from acts of violence.

Article 14

1. Efforts made by the community in order to prevent violations of Women's rights include:
a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that may cause violations of Women's rights;
b. strengthening the role of community, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. preventing unregistered marriages and siri marriages.
2. Efforts made in order to prevent violations of Children's rights include:
a. monitoring various conditions occurring in their environment that cause violations of Children's rights;
b. strengthening the role of community, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. preventing marriage at the age of Children.

Article 28

1. The Regency Government provides scholarships and/or educational assistance for:
a. children from poor families;
b. neglected children; and
c. children residing in remote areas.
2. The implementation of scholarship programs and/or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and community organizations.
3. Further provisions regarding the provision of scholarships and or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 38

1. The Regency Government provides shelters to foster street children and social institutions for neglected children.
2. Shelters as referred to in paragraph (1) may be organized in cooperation with Community Organizations.

Article 10

1. The community shall and is responsible for implementing the protection of Women and Children including:

CHAPTER VIII

CHILD PARTICIPATION

Article 55

1. Every Child has the right to participate in expressing opinions, ideas, and thoughts related to life based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
2. Child participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out through Child Forums starting from the village level, sub-district within the regency.
3. Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (2) represent Children, both geographic domicile representation, socio-cultural groups and Children's educational backgrounds.
4. The establishment of Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (2) is facilitated by the Regency Government.
5. The establishment of Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (4) is stipulated by Regent's Decree.

Article 53

1. The Regency Government provides skills training to increase Women's capacity.
2. In providing training as referred to in paragraph (1) the Regency Government may cooperate with training institutions organized by community organizations.
3. The Regency Government expands access and opportunities for Women in obtaining skills and employment.

Article 36

1. The Regency Government must organize care for neglected Children.
2. Care as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by Community Organizations in the social field.
3. In the event that a Child is neglected because for some reason the parents neglect their obligations, then the Family or Regency Government or Community Organization as referred to in paragraph (2) may submit an application to the court to determine the Child as a neglected Child.
4. The court determination as referred to in paragraph (3) simultaneously determines the shelter and care for the neglected Child concerned.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One

Definition, Understanding and Terminology Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a development system based on Children's rights through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's Rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to recognize power relationship gaps between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different. 29. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities. 30. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila. 31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree. 33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Child Protection, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking, which is established by the government or community-based.

1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a development system based on Children's rights through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's Rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 58

1. The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Women and Child Protection.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out in the form of:
a. training for government officials and law enforcers on prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and
f. increasing the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent in conducting guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of Agency.

Article 19

1. Employers who employ Women must maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.
2. Employers must place Women workers in places that are safe for Women's reproductive health.
3. Employers must fulfill the rights of Women workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
4. Employers provide special facilities for nursing mothers in their companies.

Article 20

1. Women workers/laborers aged at most 18 (eighteen) years are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant Women workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
3. Employers who employ Women workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, must:
a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and
b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace.
4. Employers must provide shuttle transportation for Women workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One

Definition, Understanding and Terminology Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a development system based on Children's rights through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's Rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 58

1. The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Women and Child Protection.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out in the form of:
a. training for government officials and law enforcers on prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and
f. increasing the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent in conducting guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of Agency.

Article 56

1. In every formulation of policies related to Children, the Regency Government considers and accommodates Children's Opinions submitted through Child Forums.
2. The Regency Government includes representatives of Child Forums in the Regency Development Planning Deliberation.

Article 36

1. The Regency Government must organize care for neglected Children.
2. Care as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by Community Organizations in the social field.
3. In the event that a Child is neglected because for some reason the parents neglect their obligations, then the Family or Regency Government or Community Organization as referred to in paragraph (2) may submit an application to the court to determine the Child as a neglected Child.
4. The court determination as referred to in paragraph (3) simultaneously determines the shelter and care for the neglected Child concerned.

Article 47

b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.

Article 47

1. The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence.
2. Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.

a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.

Definition, Understanding and Terminology Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a development system based on Children's rights through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's Rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

1. Women workers/laborers aged at most 18 (eighteen) years are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.

a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and
b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace.

CHAPTER V

Part One

Implementation of Protection of Women

Article 47

1. The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence.
2. Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for Women and Children victims of violence who need safe houses include: a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or d. neglected if not placed in a safe house.

a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 9

Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a development system based on Children's rights through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's Rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a development system based on Children's rights through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's Rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 58

1. The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Women and Child Protection.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out in the form of:
a. training for government officials and law enforcers on prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and
f. increasing the professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent in conducting guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of Agency.

Article 9

1. The Regency Government in order to carry out its responsibilities, establishes programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children with the Regional Action Plan as the basis for Regional Apparatus in implementing the protection of Women and Children.
2. Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 38

1. The Regency Government provides shelters to foster street children and social institutions for neglected children.
2. Shelters as referred to in paragraph (1) may be organized in cooperation with Community Organizations.
3. Further provisions regarding shelters as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation Article 39 The implementation of protection for Women and Children is organized by Regional Apparatus whose duties and functions are related to the protection of Women and Children.

Article 43

a. Victims;
b. Family;
c. Community; and/or
d. community organizations in the field of protection of Women and Children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and
c. by letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 42 are authorized to handle victims of violence against Women and Children obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2) are regulated by Regent Regulation

Article 47

1. The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence.
2. Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.

b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or d. neglected if not placed in a safe house.

a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHILD PARTICIPATION

Article 47

1. The Regency Government may provide safe houses for Women and Children victims of violence.
2. Safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) aim to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of safe houses as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. Criteria for Women and Children victims of violence who need safe houses include: a. their lives are threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or d. neglected if not placed in a safe house.
5. The implementation of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the implementation of safe house services are regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One

Definition, Understanding and Terminology Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Regency is Musi Banyuasin Regency. 2. Regency Government is the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 3. Regent is the Regent of Musi Banyuasin. 4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Musi Banyuasin Regency. 5. Office of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPPA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Musi Banyuasin Regency. 6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial protection (assistance and treatment). 7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 8. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb. 9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights. 10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has potential and/or special talents not limited to intellectual abilities, but also in other fields. 11. Prevention is direct efforts carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of Women's rights and Children's Rights. 12. Children's Forum is a forum for Child participation formed with the aim of facilitating the involvement of Children in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking. 13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency/City that has a development system based on Children's rights through the integration of government, community and business commitments and resources that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of Children's Rights. 14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity. 17. Human trafficking is the act of recruiting, transporting, harboring, sending, transferring, or receiving a person by threat of violence, use of violence, kidnapping, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. 18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community. 19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the abilities of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly. 20. Law enforcement is the action of officials authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations. 21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that is gender sensitive. 22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin. 23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims. 24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence according to established standards. 25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out activities of social assistance/guidance, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop normally. 26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim. 27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality. 28.

Article 51

1. Repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return Women and Children victims of violence to their area of origin.
2. Repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
3. The Regency Government carries out repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

2. The report as referred to in paragraph (1) is submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

2. Repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
3. The Regency Government carries out repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

CHAPTER VIII

CHILD PARTICIPATION

Article 55

1. Every Child has the right to participate in expressing opinions, ideas, and thoughts related to life based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
2. Child participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out through Child Forums starting from the village level, sub-district within the regency.
3. Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (2) represent Children, both geographic domicile representation, socio-cultural groups and Children's educational backgrounds.
4. The establishment of Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (2) is facilitated by the Regency Government.
5. The establishment of Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (4) is stipulated by Regent's Decree.

Paragraph 3

Employment

Article 36

1. The Regency Government must organize care for neglected Children.
2. Care as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by Community Organizations in the social field.
3. In the event that a Child is neglected because for some reason the parents neglect their obligations, then the Family or Regency Government or Community Organization as referred to in paragraph (2) may submit an application to the court to determine the Child as a neglected Child.
4. The court determination as referred to in paragraph (3) simultaneously determines the shelter and care for the neglected Child concerned.

CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 62

Implementing regulations of this Regional Regulation are stipulated no later than 1 (one) year from the promulgation of this Regional Regulation.
